subject: Cross-entity settlement schedule & collection playbook
messages:
From: Ana Torres <ana.torres@greenline.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Juan Perez <juan.perez@greenline-eu.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Billing flow for Q4 — entity split question

Hi Neha / Karthik,

Thanks for the call earlier. Per procurement and tax, we need to confirm how Redwood plans to invoice across our NA and EU entities. A few specific asks from our side:

- Can Redwood issue separate VAT invoices to Greenline Logistics (US) and Greenline Logistics EMEA (NL)?
- We prefer remittances to be routed to separate bank accounts per entity (instructions attached to each invoice).
- How will credits / refunds be handled when usage spans multiple entities in a single month?

I've attached a workbook with our Q3 invoice extracts (GL_Invoices_Q3_2026.xlsx) to illustrate the split. If you can propose a simple settlement cadence and a sample apportionment file we can validate on our side, that would help accelerate legal and treasury sign-off.

Cheers,
Ana Torres
Procurement Manager
Greenline Logistics
procure@greenline.com

Attachments: GL_Invoices_Q3_2026.xlsx (Excel spreadsheet, 240KB)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Ana Torres <ana.torres@greenline.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Billing flow for Q4 — entity split question

Hi Ana — thanks for sending the workbook. Helpful context.

Summary of what we can offer and next steps (proposed):

1) Separate tax invoices per legal entity
   - Redwood can emit distinct invoices per entity (Redwood US LLC and Redwood EU B.V.). Each invoice will include the appropriate VAT/tax line for that legal entity.

2) Remittance routing and bank accounts
   - We can include separate remittance instructions on each invoice and support distinct bank accounts per entity. We will need your preferred billing contact per entity and the account details (IBANs).

3) Apportionment and netting
   - For cross-entity usage we suggest a monthly apportionment file (CSV) that maps invoice line items to your cost centers and entities. Attached is a simple template (cross-entity-settlement-template.csv) with columns: invoice_id, line_item_id, amount, currency, entity_code.
   - Netting: Redwood can perform a soft net (reporting-level netting) and provide settlement statements for treasury to reconcile. Any inter-entity transfers / FX will be handled by your treasury; Redwood will not perform inter-company netting on your behalf unless requested under a separate SOW.

4) Credits/refunds
   - Credits will be issued to the same legal entity that was invoiced. If an invoice needs to be split across entities for a correction, we will issue corresponding credit notes and new invoices.

Next immediate asks from Greenline: billing contact + confirmed remittance accounts for each invoicing entity.

I'm looping in Karthik to confirm the implementation timeline and Marissa (Finance) to prep Redwood-side templates and GL postings. We can aim for a pilot on December invoices if we receive details this week.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0182

Attachments: cross-entity-settlement-template.csv (CSV, 3KB)

- Any constraints on including distinct remittance instructions per invoice (bank account lines) in our billing engine?
- If Greenline provides a monthly apportionment CSV (template attached), what's the simplest way for Finance to consume it? (Auto-import to AR vs manual upload)
- Any recommended language for the MSA addendum to cover split invoicing & VAT handling?

Thanks for the context — reviewed the workbook and template. Finance can support the proposed flow with the following clarifications and next steps: 

1) Billing engine capabilities
   - We can emit multiple invoices per customer account in our billing system and route separate PDFs to distinct emails. No system changes required.

2) Remittance instructions
   - We can include per-invoice remittance instructions. For wire transfers to the EU entity we need the IBAN and beneficiary name. Please have Greenline confirm IBANs for the EMEA entity.

3) Consumption of apportionment CSV
   - Preferred: they populate the template and upload to the secure SFTP we provide. We can ingest the file and auto-apply apportionments to the AR ledger. Manual upload is also possible but will create delays.
   - SFTP onboarding: please share Greenline's SFTP contact (or they can upload via the secure portal link we will send).

4) Credits / refunds
   - Credits will be issued to the invoiced legal entity. For corrections that require cross-entity reallocations, Finance will issue credit notes + re-invoices and include a memo describing the netting mechanics for their tax team.

5) Pilot schedule & deadlines
   - To hit a December pilot (invoices dated 2026-12-01), we need: confirmed billing emails and IBANs by 2026-11-19 and the first apportionment CSV by 2026-11-25.

6) Next docs and signatures
   - I'll prepare a short addendum (billing contact + entity map + SFTP credentials) and route it for signature. I'll also create a one-page playbook for Greenline treasury describing monthly steps.

Action items (owners):
- Ana / Greenline: provide billing contacts per entity + IBANs (due 2026-11-19)
- Neha: confirm pilot scope and share the HubSpot deal link with procurement (done)
- Karthik: please confirm if Sales Ops needs any extra tracking fields in the invoicing metadata (deal tags)
- Marissa: I'll attach the draft addendum and the portal link after I get Ana's contact.

Thanks — I'll attach the addendum and the playbook in my follow-up.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Finance Manager | Redwood Inference
